title: Business Insider Faces Traffic Drop and Seeks New Model
seoTitle: Business Insider Faces Traffic Drop, Eyes New Model
subtitle: Editor-in-chief reveals alarming figures and transition plans
excerpt: Amid a 78% drop in traffic, CEO Christian Baesler announces a model shift and reinforces confidence in the publication's future viability.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In a staff meeting in New York, Business Insider's new head, Christian Baesler, revealed traffic data showing a 78% drop over five years. The peak of 95 million monthly unique visitors in 2021 fell to 21 million in 2026.

Traffic drop in numbers

The figures, based on Comscore, indicate that the traffic-driven revenue model that once sustained Business Insider is unraveling. The publication, which previously relied heavily on SEO, now registers monthly traffic of 21 million users, a figure drastically lower than the 28 million from the previous year.

Internal staff reaction

One employee described the traffic loss as “dire,” while another simply reacted with “Yikes.” A third noted that the decline in 2025 was less steep, suggesting a potential rebound point, though the remark was made in a lighthearted manner.

The CEO's transition plan

Baesler stated he was “confident” in Business Insider's future and underscored the need to move away from traffic dependence. He announced a restructuring centered on franchises and newsletters, aiming to build a business that no longer relies on the flow of online visitors.

Impact on monetization platforms

In Baesler's own words, channels such as YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram remain “under-monetized.” The strategy involves tapping into other revenue streams, reducing the pressure on traditional traffic.

Market perspective

Business Insider, which has already weathered layoffs and financial challenges, is now looking to reinvent its business model. Shifting its focus toward subscription content and franchises could be crucial for its sustainability in a constantly evolving digital landscape.

With information from Status, AdExchanger, Talking Biz News.
